chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Abu al-Jarud, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'May God have mercy on a servant who revives knowledge.'
He said: I asked, 'And what is its revival?' He said: 'That he discusses it with the people of religion and the people of piety.'

key_terms.أَهْلُ الدِّينِ: People of religion — those who are committed to religious practice
key_terms.أَهْلُ الْوَرَعِ: People of piety — those characterized by religious scrupulousness and abstaining from doubtful matters
key_terms.إِحْيَاء: Revival, giving life to — the act of keeping knowledge alive through active use and transmission
key_terms.يُذَاكِرَ: To discuss, exchange, or mutually remind one another — from the root dhikr (remembrance); implies interactive scholarly dialogue

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Baqir define the revival of knowledge?
ai.summary: Abu al-Jarud reports that Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) invoked God's mercy upon any believer who revives knowledge through scholarly discussion. When asked to clarify what 'revival of knowledge' means, the Imam explained it as engaging the people of religion and piety in dialogue. In early Islamic scholarly circles, knowledge was considered a living tradition that could stagnate without active communal engagement — 'revival' (ihya') was not mere memorization but the dynamic circulation of learning among the devout.
